title.rendered: Cook claims second pole position of 2026 season

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing's Josh Cook claimed pole position for the...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing's Josh Cook claimed pole position for the second time this season after a lights-to-flag triumph in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Qualifying Race at Croft.

Cook has been one of the stars of qualifying in 2026 having scored no fewer than four front row starts from the eight race weekends so far – more than any other driver – and the Toyota star produced a commanding performance in this particular contest.

Having topped the earlier qualifying segment, Cook made a solid getaway from pole position as his rivals squabbled behind. NAPA Racing UK's Dan Cammish held second with his Ford Focus Titanium teammate Ash Sutton blasting by Tom Ingram (Team VERTU - Hyundai) and Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi).

Disaster struck for Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden in the opening exchanges when his Toyota Corolla was turned around as the 23 cars tried to settle into single file through the Esses for the first time. It was a huge disappointment for the Scotsman with the three-time champion starting the race from a promising sixth before the incident spun his machine to the back of the order.

The top three positions remained unchanged, with the other notable incidents affecting the aforementioned Ingram and Doble. First came frustration for Doble, whose Audi A3 Saloon suffered a loss of power that sent him tumbling down the pack, while a late-race error from Ingram dropped him back one position.

Ingram's Hyundai ran wide through Sunny In, allowing the WSR BMW of Daryl De Leon to nip by. The duo fought frenetically on the final lap, running side-by-side through a number of corners as Ingram nudged ahead again at one stage, before young star De Leon fought back to clinch fourth.

While the incident only cost Ingram a single point, the reigning champion can ill afford any further setbacks as he tries to reduce the ever-increasing deficit to title rival Sutton at the top of the overall Drivers' standings.

Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi), Ricky Collard (Team VERTU - Hyundai) and Dan Rowbottom (CPRL - Mercedes) were next in the order with the Restart Racing Hyundai duo of Chris Smiley and local man Dan Lloyd rounding out the top ten.

Rounds 22, 23 and 24 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at the loveable North Yorkshire venue tomorrow and it may prove to be a pivotal day in the title race as the season draws towards its final stretch.

A great crowd is expected to fill the banks and grandstands around the 2.13-mile circuit with many more watching the action on television and online around the world. Fans in the UK can watch on ITV4 from 11:15am, viewers in North America can catch every race LIVE via the RACER network, whilst the rest of the world can see every second of race day via the BTCC YouTube channel.

Josh Cook, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "It's really nice to get P1 and put us in the best place possible to start tomorrow. It may have looked calm from the outside, the car was actually quite a handful, so to hold off the Fords and bring it home is very pleasing. Ultimately, we need to make sure we convert this tomorrow. If we can get through lap one and keep the Fords behind in the early stages then I think we should be in with a good shout to replicate the result. This is Croft though and the weather can also play its part, so we just need to see what happens."

title.rendered: Rowbottom continues CPRL's successful run

excerpt.rendered: Dan Rowbottom has continued the impressive mid-season turnaround of the...

content.rendered:
Dan Rowbottom has continued the impressive mid-season turnaround of the rookie CPRL squad by topping the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Free Practice session at Croft.

The team has delivered impressive results during the previous three meetings, which began with Rowbottom's maiden podium for the outfit at Thruxton back in July. At Knockhill, teammate Adam Morgan secured victory in the Qualifying Race, as well as an outright race win, before he scored a triumphant double at Donington Park last time out.

The results underline the efforts of the team's engineers and mechanics, who have worked tirelessly to extract performance from the Mercedes A35 Saloons, and that run may look set to continue here at Croft with Rowbottom setting the pace during practice.      

Both Rowbottom and Morgan have enjoyed success at the 2.127-mile Croft Circuit in the past, with one win, three additional podium finishes and five further top-five results between them in the BTCC.

LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing's Mikey Doble was just 0.156s off the top as he looks to secure his second win of the season in the new Audi A3 Saloon, whilst NAPA Racing UK's Dan Cammish was third.

Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) made it five different manufacturers in the top five as Toyota and Hyundai also joined the party, suggesting that we're in for an unpredictable weekend.

Championship leader Ash Sutton was sixth in the #116 NAPA Racing UK Ford Focus Titanium whilst WSR's Charles Rainford ensured all six marques were covered in the top seven finishers during practice.

Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing), Daryl De Leon (WSR) and Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) rounded out the top ten.

As is now the case in 2026, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter nine lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

title.rendered: Darlington UK meets Darlington USA

excerpt.rendered: Unique weekend of action for Goodyear Racing Eagles This weekend,...

content.rendered:
Unique weekend of action for Goodyear Racing Eagles

This weekend, Goodyear Racing Eagles will be at the heart of the action at Croft Circuit in North Yorkshire for the British Touring Car Championship, one of the world's most competitive and thrilling motorsport spectacles. Simultaneously, Goodyear Racing is competing across three additional major championships globally, showcasing the technological prowess and capabilities of the Goodyear Racing Team and its Eagle tire family.

Incredibly, the BTCC race weekend takes place near to Darlington, England, which coincides with NASCAR's “Chase to the Championship” playoff opener at Darlington Raceway in South Carolina!

With the FIA World Endurance Championship's Lone Star Le Mans endurance event in Austin, Texas and the NHRA U.S. Nationals in Indianapolis taking place across the same weekend, the races will see Goodyear technology pushed to its limits.

Xavier Fraipont, Vice President, Goodyear Racing said: “Goodyear Racing is at its best when we can demonstrate just how different the demands of racing can be, and this weekend brings together four very different racing environments and demonstrates the challenges for Goodyear Racing Eagle tires across four distinct championships.

“The varied environments and challenges allow our technical teams to create tires that perform, and those lessons translate to the tires that customers can buy today. ‘Fast is in us’ isn’t just our mantra, but our fuel that allows us to create what we consider the best tires in the world, anywhere.”

title.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport ready for Croft challenge

excerpt.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport return to Kwik Fit...

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport return to Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship action this weekend for the eighth event of the 2026 campaign at Croft.

The team has its eyes on carrying its Donington Park GP momentum into the final three rounds of the season. Croft brings the BTCC to the northeast and has been a fixture on the calendar since the late ’90s. The 2.1-mile circuit, developed over more than 50 years, is renowned as one of the most technical challenges on the calendar and is often regarded as one of the truest all-round tests in the BTCC.

The circuit also holds plenty of fond memories for both Gordon Shedden and Árón Taylor-Smith. Across his illustrious career, Shedden has claimed three race victories and nine podium finishes at the Dalton-on-Tees venue. Croft was also the scene of Taylor-Smith’s double Independents victory in 2024, with the Dubliner having recorded a number of strong results at the circuit throughout his career.

Last time out at Donington Park, the Mark Blundell-led outfit recorded their highest points tally of the 2026 season so far. Shedden secured a well-deserved podium and Independents victory in the opening race of the weekend, alongside a strong haul of championship points. Combined with Taylor-Smith’s best points tally of the campaign to date, the team collected an impressive 60 points across the weekend, lifting both the Toyota-racing squad and its drivers up the championship standings.

Heading into the eighth event, Shedden sits eighth in the Drivers' Championship, with Taylor-Smith occupying 13th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport sit fourth in the Teams' Championship and second in the Independent Teams' Championship, with all focus set on continuing the strong form into the final stages of the season.

Following Saturday morning's opening 50-minute Free Practice session (10:15), Qualifying (14:05) and the 11-lap Qualifying Race (15:05), all will be set for Sunday's three races, scheduled for 12:10, 14:30 and 17:15 (BST), with all three broadcast live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer in North America and the BTCC YouTube channel everywhere else.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said: “I’m looking forward to Croft after a strong weekend at Donington, where we scored our best points haul of the season. We’ve made good progress with the car as the season has gone on, and the pace and consistency we showed there gives us confidence heading into this weekend. I’ve had some good results at Croft before, so the aim is to put everything together and come away with another strong points finish.”

Gordon Shedden (#52) said: “I’m looking forward to building on our recent form. Qualifying at the last two rounds has been really positive and has put us in a strong position going into Sunday, so we need to continue that this weekend. I’ve had good results at Croft in the past, including wins and podiums, and the aim is to carry that pace into the weekend, execute well and come away with another strong points haul to keep moving up the championship standings.”

title.rendered: WSR return to Croft as BTCC enters end-of-season run-in

excerpt.rendered: WSR return to their most successful circuit, Croft, as the...

content.rendered:
WSR return to their most successful circuit, Croft, as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship enters the final phase of the 2026 season this weekend (5/6 September).

The 18-time series champions have won 22 races at the North Yorkshire venue since it was reintroduced to the series in 1997 and no car on the grid can match the current-model BMW 3 Series’ five victories at the track.

A WSR podium lock-out and a clean sweep of victories in 2015 was one of the most dominant performances in recent BTCC history while wins have also been achieved in three of the last four visits to the track.

Daryl De Leon made his BTCC debut at Croft in 2023 and last year scored an overall podium finish as well as a double Jack Sears Trophy victory as he stormed towards the title at the end of the season in his BMW 330i M Sport.

The 21-year-old Anglo-Filipino scored his third rostrum result of the year last time out at Donington Park as he closed on the lead of the Independents’ Championship – in which he currently holds second place.

Teammate Charles Rainford is a two-time race winner in 2026, having triumphed at Snetterton and Oulton Park; a pair of circuits that share a number of characteristics with Croft and its blend of slow and fast corners.

The Horsham racer was the Jack Sears Trophy round winner at Croft last year and is WSR’s highest-placed driver in the overall standings in seventh place.

BTCC rookie Lewis Gilbert, who is competing at Croft for the first time in his racing career, endured a frustrating event at Donington as he endured a high-speed roll during the opening race.

The extensive damage to his BMW 330i M Sport and the two-week gap between events has not left sufficient time for repairs, meaning that the 22-year-old Scot, from Dalry, North Ayrshire, will switch to a spare chassis for this event.

Daryl De Leon said: “Croft was where my season started to turn around last year. I got on the podium, won the Jack Sears Trophy in two of the three races and then went on to qualify on the front row in three of the last four events after that. The podium at Donington last time out felt similar so I’m aiming to use that to hit the ground running this weekend and aim to be in contention throughout the weekend. WSR and the BMW have a great record there so I think we can be right up there if we get our strategy right.”

Charles Rainford said: “We’ve had a couple of difficult events since the summer break where we haven’t had the points we deserved thanks to circumstances beyond our control, but this is a new weekend and we have every opportunity to get back to the front and continue WSR’s mega record at Croft. The BTCC is all about fine margins and we just need things to tip a tiny amount in the other direction to have a really strong weekend like at Snetterton. Croft feels like the place to do it.”

Lewis Gilbert said: “Croft’s a new circuit for me, but one where WSR and the BMW have been really successful in recent years. After the size of the incident at Donington, the team at WSR have had to work flat-out to prepare the spare car for me for this weekend and I’m really grateful to them for their efforts. I want to see that hard work rewarded and some points finishes would be a good way to start.”

title.rendered: Croft takes centre stage as BTCC season enters final stretch

excerpt.rendered: Sutton holds commanding advantage as Ingram and Cammish lead the...

content.rendered:
Sutton holds commanding advantage as Ingram and Cammish lead the chase

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to Croft this weekend (5/6 September), with the North Yorkshire circuit hosting Rounds 22, 23 and 24 as the campaign enters its final three events.

Adam Morgan (CPRL – Mercedes) was the star of the show last time out at Donington Park GP, claiming two victories to make it three wins across the last two events, while Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) took the remaining success with his second victory of the season.

Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) continues to lead the way in the Drivers’ Championship, extending his advantage to 98 points over Tom Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai), with Cammish now just five points further back. With nine races remaining and Croft’s challenging 2.13-mile layout next on the agenda, the stakes continue to rise as the season heads towards its conclusion.

Back where it began

Croft provides familiar ground for the 2026 grid, with the North Yorkshire circuit having hosted the championship’s official pre-season test back in March. Five months and seven race weekends later, the field returns to the venue where the first clues of the campaign emerged, only now with the stakes considerably higher.

Tom Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai) initially led the way during that test with a 1m20.455s effort, before Daryl De Leon (WSR – BMW) ultimately topped the two days with a 1m20.417s lap. Underlining the pace already shown by the current field around a circuit combining high-speed commitment with a technical final sector.

The championship picture looked different when Croft hosted the BTCC 12 months ago. Ingram won the opening race to take control of the standings before Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) snatched victory in the finale following a dramatic four-car fight at the Hairpin. Ingram left North Yorkshire with an eight-point championship advantage over Sutton. This time, Sutton arrives 98 points clear.

Croft has certainly been a happy hunting ground for both. Over the last five years, Sutton has taken more victories at the circuit than any other driver with two, while Ingram’s six podium finishes lead the way during the same period. Sutton’s six career Croft triumphs are also the most of anyone on the current grid, ahead of Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) on four and Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing – Toyota) on three, with Ingram and Tom Chilton (Team VERTU – Hyundai) both having won twice.

Ingram also owns both of Croft’s lap records following his performances last season, setting the 1m20.522s Qualifying benchmark before posting a 1m21.374s fastest race lap. With nine races now remaining, the reigning champion will be looking to turn that proven Croft pace into the points required to begin reducing Sutton’s advantage.

Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) has his own important weekend ahead on home soil. The Yorkshireman finished second to Ingram in the opening race at Croft last year and now sits just five points behind the Team VERTU driver in the standings, making the battle for second every bit as significant as the pursuit of Sutton at the top.

Adam Morgan (CPRL – Mercedes) has meanwhile surged into fourth following a remarkable run of form, with three victories across Knockhill and Donington Park GP lifting him to 222 points. Behind him, only 23 points separate Ricky Collard (Team VERTU – Hyundai) in fifth and Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) in tenth.

Doble continues to lead the Independent Drivers’ standings heading into the weekend, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) remains at the head of the Jack Sears Trophy. With points again available in Saturday’s ‘Race to Pole’ before three further contests on Sunday, every opportunity becomes increasingly valuable as Croft begins the final three-event run to the 2026 finale.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be a sensational line-up of support series, as the Porsche Carrera Cup Great Britain, Porsche Sprint Challenge Great Britain, F4 British Championship certified by FIA and the MINI CHALLENGE Trophy complete the schedule of exciting races.

BTCC will be wowing the crowds both trackside and at home, with Saturday's 'Race to Pole' and the earlier qualifying session being streamed live via  ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1400, before ITV4's seven-and-a-half-hour race day broadcast gets underway at 1115 on Sunday.

Remember, continuing what started for the first time in the championship's history in 2025, the BTCC is being broadcast globally with every race being streamed live in 2026 via the BTCC YouTube Channel, whilst fans in North America can watch the action on the Racer Network. Look out for the races on Sunday starting at 1210, 1430 and 1715 (BST).

There's no place like being there, of course, and fans can purchase tickets in advance or on the gate throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Where to Watch: Croft

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to...

content.rendered:
The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to North Yorkshire’s Croft Circuit this weekend (5/6 September) for the eighth event of the year as the season builds into the latter stages.

Following another action-packed weekend at Donington Park, the BTCC heads to Croft with Ash Sutton leading the way as the 2026 campaign enters its final three events.

The weekend gets underway with Free Practice, then we go straight into qualifying. Two groups of 15-minute sessions, split according to the finishing order from Free Practice between odd and even finishing positions. The group with the fastest time will take the odd-numbered grid spots for the Qualifying Race. 15 minutes after qualifying, the pit lane opens ahead of the ‘Race for Pole’. An 11-lap race will then take place with half points awarded, as the result forms the grid for the first of the traditional trio of races on Sunday.

Last time out, the 2026 grid headed to Donington Park for the seventh race weekend of the championship. After another action-packed Saturday, culminating in the all-new ‘Race to Pole’, Adam Morgan would start Sunday from the front before converting that advantage into victory in Race 1. Dan Cammish then struck back in Race 2, taking his second victory of the season, before Morgan returned to the top step in the final contest to complete a superb Donington Park double. Championship leader Ash Sutton would meanwhile continue to add to his points tally as the season moved another step closer to its conclusion.

This weekend’s race day action will feature on the home of the BTCC, ITV4, from 1115 on Sunday (6 September), while the ITV YouTube page will host the Qualifying Race and Qualifying on Saturday (5 September) from 1400.

As in 2025, each race day of the season – including all support series’ races – will be streamed LIVE around the globe on the BTCC YouTube channel, with the exception of the UK and North America, which have existing broadcast arrangements.

The BTCC will be aired LIVE in North America (US and Canada), continuing the multi-year agreement with the RACER Network, streaming live and on demand as part of a long-term agreement with the championship.

All 30 races are scheduled to air on the main RACER channel, whilst support series’ and extended BTCC highlights will be available to watch via the RACER+ App, the network’s premium motorsports streaming platform. Race 1 will begin at 07:10 Eastern Time (ET), with Race 2 following at 09:30 ET and Race 3 closing out the day’s racing at 12:15 ET.

title.rendered: Mikey Doble shows fighting spirit at Donington Park

excerpt.rendered: Mikey Doble showcased his bounce-back ability at Donington Park GP...

content.rendered:
Mikey Doble showcased his bounce-back ability at Donington Park GP this past weekend (22/23 August) to maintain his Independents’ Trophy title charge in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

Returning to the scene of his historic victory at the start of the season, the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver battled mechanical issues that were out of the team’s control to score a brace of points-scoring finishes around the Leicestershire circuit.

Saturday proved to be a case of what might have been for the former Jack Sears Trophy title winner as an electrical gremlin scuppered his chances of securing a starting spot towards the front of the grid for Sunday’s opening encounter.

Having set the second-fastest time in practice earlier in the day, Doble entered qualifying and the ‘Race To Pole’ as one to watch; however, that soon changed as his Audi A3 Saloon ground to a halt heading up Schwantz Curve early on.

Dropping to last place, the 27-year-old was able to get his front-wheel-drive machine restarted and, thanks to a fortuitous appearance by the safety car, Doble was able to salvage a result as he fought his way back up to 14th place.

Lining up on the seventh row of the grid for race one, Doble opted to run the less preferable hard tyre in race one and, despite having to contend with a number of rivals on the medium tyre, the Surrey racer made progress as he fought his way up to tenth. 

Race two unfortunately saw the two-time race winner experience a recurrence of the issue that plagued him on Saturday. Running well inside the top ten and moving forward, Doble lost all power and frustratingly dropped to the rear of the field.

Keen to bounce back from that setback, Doble once again showcased his overtaking prowess in a feisty reverse grid encounter as he utilised the faster medium tyre to scythe his way up the order and take the chequered flag in 11th. 

Leaving Donington Park, Doble remains at the top of the Independent Drivers’ Championship holding a 30-point lead over his nearest challenger, Daryl De Leon.

Mikey Doble: “It’s probably been the first weekend this season where I’ve experienced bad luck, so although I’m disappointed that we weren’t able to come away with more, I’m content that we were able to maintain the Independents’ lead.

“On Saturday we had really good pace but the issue that hampered us in the Race To Pole meant that we had very little to show for our efforts. We opted to take the pain of the hard tyre in race one and we managed to fight our way forward which was good.

“Then with the medium tyre on for the rest of the day, I was confident we could push on but sadly the issue on Saturday popped up again and cost us in race two. To round out the day going from the back of the grid was pleasing but ultimately the warmer temperatures hampered us a little bit.

“We’re heading into the business end of the season now and the focus is on making sure we can either maintain or build the points lead we’ve got in the Independents. Looking ahead to Croft, we should go well there so I’m excited to get up to North Yorkshire.”

title.rendered: The Captured Moments: Donington Park GP

excerpt.rendered: A handpicked selection of standout images from the seventh weekend...

content.rendered:
A handpicked selection of standout images from the seventh weekend of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Donington Park.

Across three action-packed races, the 2.49-mile Grand Prix circuit delivered no shortage of memorable moments, from wheel-to-wheel battles and charges through the order to race-winning performances and one of the most dramatic incidents of the season. From the pressure of the ‘Race to Pole’ to the heavy braking zones of the Melbourne Loop, the weekend produced a constant flow of scenes worth capturing.

Rather than a full archive, this collection represents a curated edit of the most striking and atmosphere-rich frames from across the weekend, selected to reflect the intensity, character and detail that defined the event.

Adam Morgan enjoyed a remarkable weekend, following victory in the ‘Race to Pole’ with two further wins on Sunday, while Dan Cammish added another Donington Park GP triumph to become the most successful current driver around the configuration. Elsewhere, Daryl De Leon charged through the order to claim silverware, while Lewis Gilbert thankfully walked away unscathed from a huge incident in the final race.

What follows is the edit, 30 moments from Donington Park GP, presented in its defining images.

title.rendered: Season high for Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport at Donington Park

excerpt.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport enjoyed its best points-scoring...

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport enjoyed its best points-scoring weekend of the 2026 season at Donington Park (22/23 August), with a podium finish and Independent's victory for Gordon Shedden and a superb run of consistency from Árón Taylor-Smith, combining for 60 points across the weekend to lift the team and drivers up the championship tables.

The team headed to event seven looking to build on a strong run of recent results, and left Leicestershire having climbed from sixth to fourth in the Teams' Championship and from third to second in the Independent Teams' Championship, with Taylor-Smith also banking his best individual points haul of the campaign so far.

Qualifying arrived in cloudy but dry conditions, and Shedden continued his strong qualifying form from Knockhill, going second fastest in his group, while Taylor-Smith backed it up with the third-fastest time in the session. Combined across both groups, it left the Scotsman fourth on the overall qualifying order and the Irishman sixth, an excellent platform for the weekend ahead.

That set up Saturday afternoon's Qualifying Race, which determines Sunday's opening grid. Shedden crossed the line sixth and Taylor-Smith seventh, both cars keeping tidy races together to lock in a strong starting position for Round 19 on Sunday morning.

With two Safety Car periods punctuating the race, the #52 drove it home to an Independent class win, gaining three places to cross the line third overall for a superb podium finish. The #50 was right in the mix too, moving up from seventh on the grid to finish sixth overall, rounding out a solid morning for the team.

Round 20 saw Shedden start from third, but the race proved a tough encounter, as due to the regulations, he had to run the hard tyre after his third-place finish in race one and lost places through the pack to finish 13th. Taylor-Smith again delivered a consistent result, running from sixth on the grid to seventh at the flag and continuing to bank valuable points.

The third and final race of the day brought a strong response from the three-time champion, who fought back from 13th on the grid to finish sixth, a superb recovery drive to end the day with a memorable overtake on Dexter Patterson at the Melbourne Hairpin. Taylor-Smith was again the model of consistency, starting and finishing fourth to record his best individual result of the weekend.

Following the weekend, Shedden sits eighth in the Drivers' Championship, up from tenth after Knockhill, with Taylor-Smith now 13th, up from 14th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport moves up to fourth in the Teams' Championship and second in the Independent Teams' Championship, while the #52 and #50 sit third and sixth respectively in the Independents Trophy.

The team now looks ahead to the eighth event of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Croft (5/6 September).

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said: “It’s been a really positive weekend for us and, from a points perspective, it’s been my best weekend of the season so far. Qualifying sixth overall gave us a really strong platform and we were able to carry that pace into the races. To score points in all three and finish fourth in the final race is something we can be really pleased with. We’ve been consistent throughout the weekend, which is exactly what we’ve been looking for, and the 37 points I’ve scored is a great reward for the work the team has put in. We’ve got some good momentum now and I’m looking forward to taking that into Croft.”


Gordon Shedden (#52) said: “It’s been a great weekend overall. We had good pace in qualifying and to put the car fourth overall was a strong starting point, particularly after being second in our group. We then converted that into a podium and Independent win in Race One, which was exactly what we needed. Race Two was obviously a bit more difficult with the hard tyre, but we managed to regroup and fight back from P13 to P6 in the final race. To finish the weekend with a good battle and the overtake at the hairpin was a nice way to end it. We’ve scored some really important points and moved up the championship, so there are plenty of positives to take to Croft.”

title.rendered: Frustrating Donington Park weekend for Team VERTU

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU endured a weekend of frustration as the 2026...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU endured a weekend of frustration as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship headed for Donington Park GP, with a single podium finish being scant reward for the efforts of the EXCELR8-run squad.

The four-strong Hyundai team made the trip to the East Midlands venue in confident mood given a strong recent record at the circuit, with Tom Ingram, Tom Chilton, Ricky Collard and Nicolas Hamilton all optimistic about their chances on track.

Ingram and Chilton would both take part in the first qualifying session ahead of the qualifying race, with Chilton setting the sixth-best time, translating to 11th for the Race to Pole grid, but Ingram back in ninth having lost his quickest time to track limits, leaving him to start 17th.

Running in the second session, Collard was eighth fastest, leaving him to start 16th, having also fallen foul of track limits, with Hamilton going nearly a second quicker than in practice to finish in tenth, to start 20th.

Chilton therefore led the team’s challenge going into the Qualifying Race, rising up into ninth spot early on as Ingram and Collard both made up ground to move towards the top ten.

Hamilton, however, would see his challenge end before the lights went out, with a gearbox issue forcing him into the pits at the end of the green flag lap to retire.

Having moved into eighth after an early caution period, Chilton’s hope of further progress was hampered by an electrical issue that saw him briefly lose power and drop to the rear of the field, leaving Ingram to take up the challenge.

A battling drive from the champion saw him take the flag in eighth, just missing out on seventh after a race to the line with the Toyota of Aron Taylor-Smith. Collard would take the flag three spots back in eleventh, having gained five places from his starting position.

All four drivers elected to run the hard tyre in the first race of the weekend on Sunday morning, which went behind the safety car after an incident involving Chilton and Lewis Gilbert's WSR-run BMW on the opening lap.

Once the action was finally able to get underway, it was Ingram who headed the team’s challenge early on before Collard moved ahead at the Esses, with the pair running together to finish in eighth and ninth amongst the leading runners on the hard tyre.

Hamilton gained six places from where he started to finish on the fringes of the points in 17th, but it would be a tough race for Chilton as the gremlins he had faced in the Qualifying Race returned - leading to his car cutting out mid-way through the race to again drop him to the back of the field.

Switching to the medium tyre for race two, all four drivers were confident of making forward progress, with Ingram fighting his way ahead of Collard on lap one and rising to fourth by the midway point.

Having gone wheel-to-wheel with title rival Ash Sutton and Dan Rowbottom, Ingram fought hard to take third spot and add to his podium tally, with Collard two places back in fifth after emerging on top of a late battle with Dexter Patterson that saw him overhaul the Audi on the final lap.

From the back of the field, Chilton showed the pace in his car to race his way through to 14th and finish inside the points, with Hamilton battling back from a clutch issue that saw him slow away from the line to race his way to 18th spot.

The final race of the weekend would prove to be a challenge for the team, although it started well as Ingram rose into the top five in the early stages, before dropping down the order when title rival Ash Sutton collided with him at the Old Hairpin.

Having then been forced off again later in the race, Ingram ended the weekend with an unrepresentative ninth place as the only one of the four Team VERTU drivers to score.

Contact between other drivers hampered Collard’s challenge before he pitted having suffered a puncture, with further electrical gremlins hampering Chilton as he finished back in 17th.

That was one spot behind Hamilton, who missed out on a points finish by just a tenth of a second after a race-long battle with Dan Cammish, race two's victor.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Results-wise, this has been a weekend to forget with a number of electrical issues that were outside our control, and which prevented us from making the most of the pace we had in the car.

“In the qualifying race we set the third fastest lap and we were the second quickest car out there in race three, but we’ve just had an unbelievable amount of bad luck – and weren’t the only ones.

“The team continues to work hard and gave me a package that I felt was capable of winning a race, so it’s frustrating that we weren’t able to build on the victory at Knockhill. This is a weekend to put behind us, and move on.”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“We had a decent start to race day with eighth place on the hard tyre, and a solid result in race two should have set us up for a decent run in race three from sixth on the grid.

“Sadly we got driven off the track and ended up with a puncture that put us into retirement, and it’s frustrating to have lost points as a result of that as it’s cost us a position in the standings.

“Hopefully we can be in contention at the front when we go to Croft in a couple of weeks and bounce back.”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“Pace wise I’ve been a lot quicker this weekend than I have been before but it’s been a challenging weekend – and I think that’s true for the whole team.

“Having the gearbox issue in the qualifying race did have an impact as it cost us quite a bit of track time, but I pushed my hardest in the three races and we were close to getting a point in the final race after a great battle with Dan – who managed to get the final point by a tenth of a second.

“I think what we’re discovering now is that we’re getting to the limit of the modifications I run on my car as I’ve used some of them for ten years now.

"Under braking in particular is where I’m losing time and that’s important round here, so I think the goal now is on trying to end this season as strongly as possible and then we can focus on how we improve my modifications for next year.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said:

“It’s been a really difficult weekend and I was certainly hoping to come away from Donington Park GP with a lot more than we have given our recent record. We were scratching our heads a bit after qualifying because the car felt good but just didn’t have pace, although we were able to gain ground in the qualifying race itself.

“Running the hard tyre in race one should have opened the door for strong results in races two and three but we just lacking that last little bit of pace and in race two, even though I held back some of my TTB, I couldn’t make the most of it despite the car feeling really nice and doing what I asked it to do.

“The contact with Ash in race three then left us vulnerable to people with more boost than we had, and it’s also more difficult to be in the pack and not able to benefit from clear air.

“All we can do is continue to push hard over the remaining three rounds to score as many points as possible, and look to end the season strongly – starting in a few weeks at Croft.”

excerpt.rendered: The BTCC returned to Donington Park for the seventh event...

content.rendered:
The BTCC returned to Donington Park for the seventh event of the year, showcasing three spectacular races plus another thrilling Qualifying race in Scotland. The GP layout proved an important weekend in the story of the 2026 campaign.

As the season continues towards the climax of the season, take a listen to the seventh instalment of Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed, which was aired earlier this week (Tuesday, 25 August).

The podcast opened with none other than Adam Morgan (CPRL), as the Lancastrian returned as the opening guest after taking two wins over the weekend, becoming only the second driver to take three victories this year. The #33 has also been the top scorer over the previous two events, taking 120 points out of a possible 152 over the two events.

Lewis Gilbert (WSR) was the next guest on the show, speaking on his first-lap crash that saw the BMW 330i M Sport roll. The young Scot also spoke on his first three events in tin top racing and the adjustments he has had to make after racing single-seaters.

Alan Hyde also caught up with Sam Riches (BTCC Technical Director) to discuss how the rules are designed so that incidents like Gilbert's mean drivers walk away unscathed. Ryan Bensley (Speedworks Corolla Racing) was next on the show talking about how 'tough' the championship is. The Tin Top Tuesday debutant takes us behind the scenes of his racing life that has brought him to become a BTCC driver.

BTCC returnee Daniel Lloyd made a shock appearance after not expecting to race in 2026. The Huddersfield racer spoke on his unfortunate weekend, after a gear lever snapped in practice and the car caught fire in the second race on Sunday. Mark Tyler was the final guest of the show, someone who has worked with the TOCA Safety team since 2003.

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship grid heads to Croft (5/6 September) for the annual visit to the Yorkshire venue for the seventh race weekend of the campaign.

title.rendered: De Leon saves best till last with charge to Donington podium

excerpt.rendered: WSR’s Daryl De Leon scorched to an inspired third place...

content.rendered:
WSR’s Daryl De Leon scorched to an inspired third place in the final race of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship weekend at Donington Park last Sunday (23 August).

The 21-year-old Anglo-Filipino had to work hard for his third podium finish of the season, having to race through from the sixth row of the grid following a weekend blighted by misfortune.

De Leon retired from the Qualifying Race with an electronic issue, which meant he had to start from the back of the grid in Race One, where he made up six places.

The reigning Jack Sears Trophy champion produced another charge in Race Two, forging through to 11th, and that meant he was at least within sight of the leaders when he began the final race of the day.

Jumping two places at the start, he latched on to a battle that included reigning title-holder Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) and Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport). The #2 fought his way past them all and, finally, claimed third on lap nine.

The result means the Cambridgeshire-based driver stays second in the Independents Drivers’ standings and closes to within 30 points of leader Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing).

Teammate Charles Rainford started alongside De Leon on the grid for Race Three, in 12th, and produced a similarly swashbuckling performance to battle through to fifth place at the flag.

Tracking behind De Leon, he was embroiled in the multi-champion pack and satisfyingly took fifth place from Shedden at Goddards on the final lap.

Rainford’s weekend was also a story of recovery after an issue in qualifying meant he started 15th for Race One, finishing 12th. In both the first and second races of the day he found himself off the track on the opening lap, and thus racing back through to 12th again in Race Two.

The Horsham driver now sits seventh in the overall Drivers’ Standings with three rounds still to go at Croft, Silverstone and Brands Hatch respectively.

Scottish rookie Lewis Gilbert’s race day lasted less than a lap when he was involved in a collision just before the Melbourne Hairpin and was launched into a terrifying barrel roll.

The BMW 330i M Sport withstood the accident well enough for Gilbert to emerge unscathed, but the resultant damage meant he took no further part in the weekend.

The three WSR drivers and the rest of the 2026 grid return to action at Croft in less than two weeks (5/6 September).

Daryl De Leon: “It’s been a tough weekend, but it ended well! We had strong pace in qualifying, ultimately placing tenth. We were running eighth in the qualifying race when I had an electrical failure not of our making, which meant I had to start from the back of the grid of Race One. It was a difficult race on the hard tyre but we managed to finish 16th. Race Two I had the mediums on and managed to make some forward progress again finishing 11th, which I was happy with. Then in the last race the car just came alive and I raced through to a podium. That’s another one to add to this year. Motor racing is tough, so the five percent that is success feels sweet.”

Charles Rainford: “This was a weekend that got away from us. We had good pace in practice and qualifying. Then in qualifying we had a brake failure, and then in the qualifying race I couldn’t really make something happen. I made a good start in Race One, but got shuffled off wide at the Old Hairpin and had to make my way back through the field again. Race Two I just kept getting hit! In Race Three I got my elbows out and we got a fifth-place finish. We dropped down a little bit in the championship, but weirdly I’m a little excited about that because it means we get almost full boost allocation, and at Croft we can work with that!”

Lewis Gilbert: “There's not that much to say. My weekend ended before it really got started! I was tagged from behind which sent me into the wall on the run to the Melbourne Hairpin and it resulted in a big accident. I’m very thankful to WSR and BMW for building such a strong car. I feel completely fine. I’m just sad for the team because there is a lot of work to do to repair the car. I’m looking forward to going to Croft and going racing again.”

title.rendered: Morgan's moment to shine

excerpt.rendered: Mercedes double plus a win for Cammish at Donington Park...

content.rendered:
Mercedes double plus a win for Cammish at Donington Park

Adam Morgan has enjoyed arguably the finest fortnight of his Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship career to date, with the CPRL driver claiming two wins at Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) after taking his first victory of the season at Knockhill last time out.

Not only has the Mercedes man claimed three race victories in recent weeks, but he has also doubled his pole position tally, having topped qualifying at each of the last two events after previously taking just one pole, back in 2018.

It was also a memorable day for Dan Cammish, as the NAPA Racing UK driver took his second win of the season to strengthen his championship challenge, moving to within five points of second-placed Tom Ingram in the overall Drivers’ standings.

A strong collection of points for Ash Sutton still sees the four-time champion hold a comfortable margin at the top of the order, whilst his Alliance Racing/Ford and NAPA Racing UK outfit further extended their advantage in the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ tables.

The Power Maxed Racing stable continues to enjoy a stellar season with its quartet of all-new Audi A3 Saloons, as Mikey Doble leads the Independent Drivers’, Dexter Patterson tops the Jack Sears Trophy and LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing hold sway in the Independent Teams’ order.

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship continues its run towards the final stretch of the season with the next event taking place at Croft Circuit in North Yorkshire in two weeks’ time (5/6 September).

Morgan converts pole into emphatic win

Following his 'Race to Pole' triumph at the famous Leicestershire circuit on Saturday, Morgan duly converted that success into a commanding victory in the first race on Sunday.

The squabble for second arguably helped as teammate Dan Rowbottom (CPRL – Mercedes) initially lost out to Speedworks Corolla Racing's Josh Cook and then current championship leader Sutton in his #116 NAPA Racing UK Ford Focus Titanium.

The opening lap provided one of the most dramatic moments of the season so far when Lewis Gilbert's WSR BMW speared off into the barrier on the approach to the Melbourne Loop. The BMW 330i M Sport then dug into the grass before barrel rolling aggressively and coming to a halt.

A shaken Gilbert was given the all clear by the TOCA Medical Team shortly after although of course still taken to the Medical Centre for further observation, whilst the same condition couldn't be said for his stricken Bavarian machine.

Morgan led away following the restart with Cook's Toyota Corolla in a good second place, whilst Sutton and Rowbottom fought behind.

Disaster struck for Cook, however, when a throttle issue slowed his car into retirement.

Sutton defended valiantly from Rowbottom with the latter eventually relinquishing third to Gordon Shedden in his Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport Toyota. Another place was given up on the final tour when Cammish's NAPA Racing UK Ford muscled past the Mercedes for fourth.

Cammish collects second win of 2026 campaign

Among the current grid, Cammish has now claimed more victories on the famed Donington Park Grand Prix circuit than any other driver, with three wins putting him clear of title rivals Sutton and Ingram.

Coincidentally, it was the same three drivers filing the podium positions in this particular race as the trio got the better of early leader Rowbottom in his CPRL Mercedes.

Cammish made his move at the final corner shortly before mid-distance as the #27 Ford Focus Titanium brushed his way through and into the lead.

Rowbottom initially fought back before dropping into the clutches of Sutton, who was impressively keeping pace despite running minimal boost and the Goodyear hard tyre compound on his NAPA Racing UK Ford. Rowbottom then slowed exiting the chicane late on and was soon shuffled further down the order by Sutton and Ingram.

The #32 Mercedes held on to fourth from the chasing Ricky Collard (Team VERTU – Hyundai) and Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi), the latter again impressively taking Independents' and Jack Sears Trophy honours.

Mighty Morgan strikes again

CPRL's Morgan was again triumphant in the Donington Park finale, becoming only the second driver to take three victories so far this season.

Morgan’s Mercedes applied pressure to pole-sitter Chris Smiley from the start, as the Restart Racing Hyundai driver worked hard to keep those behind at bay.

Smiley’s defence didn't last long however, as Morgan blasted by and immediately set about pulling away, which he duly did with consummate ease.

When the chequered flag fell Morgan had romped clear to win from the brilliant Aiden Moffat in the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi, with the latter receiving huge applause from his PMR squad and fans.

Young Daryl De Leon completed the podium positions as he provided some respite for the WSR team. A destroyed BMW earlier in the day and mixed results for their trio of drivers had provided frustrations at the Leicestershire circuit, but De Leon produced the goods in the finale to score a richly deserved podium.

CPRL's Adam Morgan was triumphant in Round 21 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Donington Park, becoming only the second driver to take three victories this season.

Morgan's Mercedes harassed pole-sitter Chris Smiley from the off, as the Restart Racing Hyundai tried desperately to fend off those behind.

His defence didn't last long as Morgan blasted by and immediately set about pulling away, which he duly did with consummate ease.

title.rendered: Adam Morgan does the double!

excerpt.rendered: CPRL driver tops teammate Dan Rowbotton in Donington Park Qualifying...

content.rendered:
CPRL driver tops teammate Dan Rowbotton in Donington Park Qualifying Race

It was a Mercedes one-two in today's Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship 'Race to Pole' around the legendary Donington Park GP circuit as Adam Morgan topped CPRL teammate Dan Rowbottom.

Incredibly, Morgan has doubled his BTCC career pole positions in just two weeks, having secured P1 at Knockhill last time out. Prior to that, the Lancastrian's only qualifying top spot came at Rockingham way back in 2018.

The result highlights the incredble progress made by the pair of Mercedes A35 Saloons since the mid-summer break.

Rowbottom secured the car's first overall podium at Thruxton in July before four more followed in the trip north of the border, including Morgan's first win of the season.

Starting the Donington Park GP Qualifying Race from pole and third respectively handed the CPRL outfit another great opportunity to impress and their situation was immediately enhanced when Rowbottom nipped by front-row starter Josh Cook on the run down to Redgate.

Cook kept Rowbottom honest during a couple of restarts, but the latter fended off the #66 Speedworks Corolla Racing machine to secure the place.

Multiple race winner Cook ended up having to go quite defensive towards the finish as the always charging Ash Sutton filled his mirrors in the #116 NAPA Racing UK Ford Focus Titanium.

Sutton had to settle for fourth, but it still represented a solid improvement from seventh on the grid as he ultimately extended his championship advantage.

Just over a second separated fifth to ninth in the order as Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) kept the Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport duo of Gordon Shedden and Árón Taylor-Smith at bay, as they – like Cook – showed the pace of the Toyota Corollas at their home track.

Tom Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai) and Sam Osborne (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) were eighth and ninth respectively, whilst Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) continued his good form with another top ten finish.

Rounds 19, 20 and 21 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at Donington Park tomorrow with the action getting underway on ITV4 at 1100.

title.rendered: Ingram tops free practice at Donington Park GP

excerpt.rendered: Tom Ingram made his pace clear in the weekend’s only...

content.rendered:
Tom Ingram made his pace clear in the weekend’s only Free Practice session as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship descended on the Donington Park GP Circuit.

The fast and frenetic 50-minute session saw all 23 cars take to the track, completing hundreds of miles around the famous Leicestershire venue.

There was one stoppage during the single practice session as Josh Cook's Speedworks Corolla Racing's machine came to a halt after the Old Hairpin. The momentary pause saw Charles Rainford's WSR BMW lead the way, but the times came tumbling down after the green flag waved once more.

When the chequered flag fell it was Mikey Doble second behind Ingram, ahead of Dan Rowbottom (CPRL), Rainford and Knockhill race winner Adam Morgan (CPRL).

As a reminder, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter nine lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

Tom Ingram, Team VERTU, said:
